hints.content:
###Getting started

**Key idea:** Parallel lines have the same slope.

###Step 1: Find the slope

Slope of the given line:

>$\blueD{0.6}$

Slope of the parallel line:

>$\purpleC{0.6}$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Two lines slant up from left to right. Both move up three units and to the right five units.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Substitute the known point into linear equation

The parallel line will have a slope of $\purpleC{0.6}$ and pass through the point $\redD{(-3,-5)}$.  Let's start from the point-slope form of the equation of the parallel line, then solve for $y$.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

>$\begin{align}
y-\redD{(-5)} &= \purpleC{0.6}(x-\redD{(-3)})\\\\\\
y+5 &= \purpleC{0.6}x +1.8 \\\\\\
y &= \purpleC{0.6}x \greenD{-3.2}
\end{align}$

options.explanation:
The **point-slope form** of a linear equation is a rearrangement of the slope formula.

>$\begin{align}
m &= \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} \\\\\\
m(x_2 - x_1) &= y_2 - y_1 \\\\\\
m(x - x_1) &= y - y_1 &&\text{Generalize.}\\\\\\
\end{align}$

This equation is true for any point $(x, y)$ on a given line, where $(x_1,y_1)$ is also a point on the line.

hints.content:
###Answer

The equation of the parallel line is $y = \purpleC{0.6}x \greenD{-3.2}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Two lines slant up from left to right. The first line is at three at the y axis and moves up three units and to the right five units. The second line has a point at negative three, negative five and moves up three units and to the right five units.

question.content:
